author: Andrew Newland
title: Indiana Governor takes aim at rising utility costs - NewsBreak
text:
By Andrew Newland Ann Powell ,
1 hours ago
EVANSVILLE, Ind. (WEHT) — Christopher Norrick is an organizer with the group Direction Against CenterPoint and says today’s announcement, a commissioner appointment to help address utility costs in the Hoosier state, was unexpected.
“This is a small step but seeing acknowledgement from the governor is positive,” Norrick said. “The strong language used in the press release was surprising”
In a release, Indiana Governor Mike Braun says “We can’t take it anymore.” The governor selected Abby Gray, a Hoosier advocate, and chose her for the new office of the utility consumer counselor commissioner. Braun also directed the office to evaluate the profits of all utility companies that operate in Indiana and find ways to ease the financial burden on Hoosiers.
“This is a good sign, however words are cheap and we have heard a lot of words and no change has happened,” Norrick said.
A rate increase for CenterPoint customers was approved last year after a high profile process. CenterPoint officials decided to phase it in over several years to help minimize the impact on customers. CenterPoint has said there are several ways customers can get help with paying utility bills.
But customers have said that it is not enough and have held several protests and public meetings regarding rising costs. Norrick says today’s announcement could be enough fuel to shed light on the issue at the state level. But he says it will be hard.
“The OUCC has been doing this work for a long time,” Norrick said. They are the state-funded representative for all rate payers and rate cases. Unfortunately, I think they are outmatched. Because of the state-funded lawyers that are going up against monopoly utility companies.”
CenterPoint response Eyewitness News obtained a statement from CenterPoint’s Senior Vice President, External Affairs. Below is the full statement:
“We hear our customers’ concerns and are deeply committed to serving their energy needs, improving the energy systems they rely on, and taking the necessary steps to keep energy rates affordable. We greatly appreciate Governor Braun’s leadership, and are committed to working with his team, state regulators, the Office of Utility Consumer Counselor and the local community on how we can work together to best prioritize our shared commitment to affordability and to continuing the investments critical to improving reliability, strengthening the energy system against extreme weather, and supporting the economic growth and development that is vital to our customers and communities. “
